identity.name: HARIOM PIPE INDUSTRIES L
identity.industry: Steel Pipes & Integrated Long Products / Energy Transition

summary.oneLiner: Hariom Pipe delivered steady Q3FY26 with 21% YoY volume growth and stable ~12.5% EBITDA margins, supported by high value-added mix (96-97%) and anti-dumping duties protecting domestic pricing. Management guides for strong Q4 (90-95k tons) and reaffirms 30% volume CAGR through FY27 driven by OEM penetration and solar capacity commissioning, though PAT growth remains capped near-term by lease accounting (ROU) depreciation and interest costs.

one-line thesis: Hariom Pipe delivered steady Q3FY26 with 21% YoY volume growth and stable ~12.5% EBITDA margins, supported by high value-added mix (96-97%) and anti-dumping duties protecting domestic pricing. Management guides for strong Q4 (90-95k tons) and reaffirms 30% volume CAGR through FY27 driven by OEM penetration and solar capacity commissioning, though PAT growth remains capped near-term by lease accounting (ROU) depreciation and interest costs.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 362.9cr (Q3, +21% YoY), INR 1,159.7cr (9M, +21% YoY); EBITDA: INR 45.2cr (Q3, 12.47% margin), INR 145.5cr (9M, 12.55% margin); PAT: INR 11.6cr (Q3, +5-6% YoY), INR 45.6cr (9M); Order Book: Not disclosed (demand visibility described as 'healthy'); Net Debt: Not explicitly stated, but finance cost ~7.79% on WC; One-offs: Depreciation spike due to Right-of-Use (ROU) assets from Ultra Pipes lease (Ind AS impact, non-cash EIR adjustment ~13% of finance cost).
guidance: Volume Growth: 30% CAGR target for FY27/FY30; Q4 Volume: 90,000-95,000 tons; Realization: INR 54,500-55,000/ton expected in Q4; Margins: Steady state EBITDA/ton INR 7,000-8,000; Solar: 35MW by Apr '26, remaining 25MW by Aug '26.
order book & pipeline: Management cites 'healthy demand visibility' and strong repeat customers in South India (Karnataka, Kerala, Andhra); no specific tonnage order book disclosed; focus shifting to B2B/OEM (now 21% of sales vs 15% previously) and government tenders.
segment / subsidiary detail: Galvanized Pipes/Coils: Primary contributor, Telangana & Tamil Nadu units stable; Integrated Steel Plant (Telangana): Near-optimal utilization; GP Utilization: ~50% (122k tons in 9M), scope for margin expansion as volume scales; Sponge Iron: Anantapur unit feeding Hyderabad, potential EC clearance pending for expansion.
growth verticals / optionality: 1) Solar Subsidiary (60MW) starting Apr '26 adding non-cyclical cash flows; 2) Metal Mart subsidiary enabling low-risk trading penetration in North/West India and OEM product gaps; 3) Potential pipe mill near Anantapur if market conditions align; 4) Gadchiroli steel plant MOU signed but land allocation delayed (1.5-2 years out).
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA/ton dipped slightly to INR 6,613 (Q3) from INR 7,039 (9M avg) due to raw material price fluctuations vs finished goods; Management expects steady state INR 7k-8k/ton; GP margins lower than MS tubes due to purchased HR coil input; Depreciation elevated due to ROU assets (Ultra Pipes lease).
capex / expansion: Solar: 60MW project progressing, land secured (including govt land); Gadchiroli: Waiting on land allotment from MSDCL, no aggressive movement expected for 1.5-2 years; Organic expansion focused on value-added products rather than greenfield mega-projects immediately.
capital allocation: Prioritizing organic capacity utilization and value-added mix; Solar project funded via project finance (implied); Trading subsidiary (Metal Mart) launched with minimal capex to test markets; No dividend commentary provided.
risks & watch-items: 1) Delay in Gadchiroli land allocation and environmental clearances; 2) PAT growth lagging revenue due to high non-cash depreciation (ROU) and interest costs; 3) Potential margin dilution from new trading subsidiary (Metal Mart) at consolidated level; 4) Raw material volatility despite anti-dumping duties.
management quality / tone: Confident and disciplined; emphasizing 'steady execution' over aggressive leaps; transparent about accounting distortions (ROU depreciation) affecting PAT; bullish on Q4 seasonality and anti-dumping benefits.
non-obvious takeaways: Creation of 'Metal Mart' subsidiary is a governance move to segregate low-margin trading revenue from high-margin manufacturing to protect reported EBITDA % clarity; ~13% of finance cost is non-cash EIR adjustment on leases, masking true cash profitability; Solar project expected to be 'near breakeven' initially due to depreciation, but cash-flow positive.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Domestic steel pipe makers face cheap imports eroding margins | Hariom Pipe Industries | beneficiary | High | Anti-dumping duties explicitly cited by MD as beneficial; company guides INR 7k-8k EBITDA/ton steady state. |
| OEMs need diverse steel products beyond pipes which Hariom doesn't manufacture | Metal Mart Pvt Ltd (Subsidiary) | beneficiary | Med | New trading arm allows Hariom to serve OEMs without distorting manufacturing margins; tests North/West markets. |
| High capex and cyclicality of pure-play steel | Hariom Power and Energy | beneficiary | Med | 60MW solar project diversifies cash flows, expected to commission 35MW by Apr '26 with minimal cash cost impact. |

themes.title: Steel tubes & building-materials capex beneficiaries
themes.need: Domestic capex + import-substitution lift value-added steel tubes/pipes and building materials - APLAPOLLO/HITECH/JTLIND/SURYAROSNI/SAMBHV/VENUSPIPES on structural & SS tubes (solar structures, DC cooling, API), FINPIPE/SUPREMEIND/APOLLOPIPE on PVC pipes, MAANALU on aluminium extrusions, RATNAVEER on SS fasteners. A data-center-cooling adjacency adds margin optionality.
themes.driver: Capex commissioning converting to volume; solar-structure & infra demand; commodity pass-through.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Focuses exclusively on the specialized 0.3-2.5mm thin steel segment (~15% of India's total steel consumption), holding a commanding 13% market share (FY25) while deliberately avoiding direct competition with heavier-pipe producers.
- Leading vertically integrated iron & steel manufacturer with strong presence in Southern & Western India, 18+ years of industry experience and 30+ years of promoters' domain expertise.
- High-Value Products contribute ~98% of sales value; in Q1FY27 they made up 96.4% of sales volume and 97.5% of revenue, with OEM Products and MS Tubes alone contributing 95.9% of revenue.
- Extensive distribution moat: 900+ dealers/B2B clients, ~80% sales through the dealer network (~20% direct B2B), with strong presence across Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Kerala and Maharashtra.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Regulatory] The Tamil Nadu Pollution Control Board suspended the previous closure directions on the Perundurai Unit and restored power supply with immediate effect (proceedings dated July 13, 2026), and operations have since recommenced.
- [Corporate history] Incorporated in 2007 as Hari Om Concast and Steels Private Limited; converted to a public limited company and renamed Hariom Pipe Industries Limited in 2018; acquired a Sponge Iron unit at Anantapur (36,000 MTPA) in 2020 and GP/GI operating assets (180,000 MTPA, Tamil Nadu) in 2023.
